checks.comparison: Method 4 event by event. 'Ask all workers at x^k / Init g_i = 0, B_i = 0' corresponds to the initial state and the round-end reset (starts all t, counts/sums 0). 'while HM(B) < S/n: wait for the next worker j' is one template call to eventOracle returning the earliest finisher. 'B_j += 1; receive grad f_j(x^k; xi^k_{j,B_j}); g_j += it' is step's B and G update with the gradient g e.1 x (seed r (code n j B_j)). 'Ask this worker again at x^k' is update starts i t. The exit test is harmonicReady, checked after each event. step: on reply (i, t, g), B := counts with B_i + 1 and G := sums with G_i + g. If harmonicReady n S B, then x := point - gamma ((1/n) sum_j (1/B_j) G_j); the new state has round + 1, counts and sums reset to 0, point x, all starts t, clock t, and selected x if chosen = round + 1. Otherwise the counts and sums are updated, worker i restarts at t (Function.update starts i t), the clock is t and the point is unchanged. On none the state is unchanged. harmonicReady n S B := (forall i, 1 <= B i) and (S : R)/n <= ((1/n) * sum_i 1/(B i : R))^{-1}.

The uniform random iterate among x^0..x^K plus the elapsed time is the eps-stationary output. malenia p: Seed Fin (K+1) with uniform law; initial j = (round 0, counts 0, sums 0, point x0, starts 0, clock 0, chosen j, selected x0); query = none once K <= round, else some (point, starts, round, counts); update = identity once K <= round, else step; output (selected, clock).

g^k = (1/n) sum_i (1/B_i) g_i^k; x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma g^k; stop all workers. This is the harmonicReady branch: x = point - gamma ((1/n) sum_j (1/B_j) G_j), with all workers restarted at t (stop and re-ask at the new point).

Line 2340: x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma (1/n) sum_j (1/B_j) sum_{i<=B_j} grad f_j(x^k; xi^k_{j,i}). estimator B g x omega = (1/n) * sum_i (1/B_i) * sum_{j < B_i} g_i(x, omega(code n i j)), with code n i j = j*n + i (injective on Fin n x Nat). sgdIterate G gamma x0 seeds gives y_{r+1} = y_r - gamma G_r(y_r, seeds r). iterate g gamma B x0 seeds = sgdIterate (fun r => estimator (B r) g) gamma x0 seeds. iterOracle p n B P g: Seed r = (Nat -> Omega); law = map arrays P (the call-r seed is the round-r array arrays xi r); answer r x seed = estimator (B r) g x seed.

The finishing worker j returns grad f_j(x^k; xi^k_{j,B_j}) of its local function, sampled from round k's array. eventAnswer p V g (some (x, starts, r, B)) seed returns the earliest finishing worker e.1 (RennalaUniform.earliest of completion (V i) (starts i)) with its finish time e.2 and the gradient g e.1 x (seed r (code n e.1 (B e.1))). Here B e.1 is the pre-increment (0-based) count, so this is the (B+1)-th gradient of that worker in round r, i.e. xi^r_{i,B_i} of Method 4 line 519. If no worker finishes the reply is none, and on query none it is none. eventOracle: Seed k = (Nat -> Nat -> Omega) for every call; law = map (fun xi _ => arrays xi) P (every call sees the same round arrays); answer = eventAnswer. arrays xi r c = xi (Nat.pair r c).

eq:upper_bound for general (W, eta). roundTime V eta s = ofReal (sInf {t | 0 <= t and (forall i, 1 <= floor(V_i t - V_i s)) and eta <= ((1/n) sum_i 1/floor_i)^{-1}}) if that set is nonempty, else top; deadline 0 = 0, deadline (k+1) = top if deadline k = top, else roundTime V eta (deadline k).toReal.

The harmonic exit test uses real casts. The conjunct forall i, 1 <= B i is essential, because Lean's 1/0 = 0 would otherwise inflate the harmonic mean. It implements the source convention (1/0 = infinity makes the while condition true while any B_i = 0). Checking after each event is equivalent to the while loop, since the condition is false initially. Ties go to the lowest index (valid ordering of simultaneous completions). Nothing else is added.
The uniform index is independent of the samples and the clock is the last event time; the output is accepted, as for Theorem 5.3.
Exactly the source step; nothing more.

One call per round with counts B r, and an independent array per round (positions Nat.pair r c of an IID stream). The 0-based j < B_i matches 1..B_i. The constructed IsProbabilityMeasure proof (iterOracle._proof_1, standard axioms) confirms arrays is measurable, so the map is a genuine pushforward.

The gradient is taken at the queried current point q.1; under the pinned malenia every running computation in round r started at that point (accepted interpretation). Every call sees the same arrays (diagonal law), so each (round, worker, count) uses one fixed stream position. The probability-measure proof confirms measurability. The oracle trusts the start times and counts supplied by the pinned algorithm.
The 'all floors >= 1' encoding equals the source set for non-decreasing W and eta > 0 (accepted interpretation). Floors are Int casts to R; toReal is only applied to a finite deadline.

The reply worker is the one whose count/sum is updated and who restarts; the sample index (round r, code n i B_i) matches the estimator's omega(code n i j) with omega = arrays xi r, so the event iterate equals iterate g gamma B x0 (arrays xi).
Classical decidability is used for harmonicReady and the existence test. The polarities are correct: exit when HM >= S/n; roundTime is the infimum of the set where the condition holds.
